en: The Question on the Arising of Formations (Saṅkhāra)
“Venerable Nāgasena, are there any conditioned phenomena (saṅkhārā) that are born?
“Yes, Great King, there are conditioned phenomena that are born.”
“When there is the eye, O Great King, and forms, visual consciousness arises; when there is visual consciousness, visual contact arises;
when there is visual contact, feeling arises; when there is feeling, craving arises.”
When there is craving, clinging comes to be; when there is clinging, existence comes to be; when there is existence, birth comes to be;
when there is birth, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be.
Such is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.
Moreover, Great King, when the eye does not exist and visible forms do not exist, eye-consciousness does not arise; when eye-consciousness does not exist, eye-contact does not arise;
when eye-contact does not exist, feeling does not arise; when feeling does not exist, craving does not arise;
when craving does not exist, clinging does not arise; when clinging does not exist, becoming does not arise. When becoming...
"When there is no birth, there is no aging and death; when there is no birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair do not come to be.
Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering.
The fourth question: On that which is being born from volitional formations.
